documents.generated_document: RADIATION ONCOLOGY - TREATMENT PLAN SUMMARY. PATIENT: John Doe. MRN: 9982314. DATE: 10/24/2023. ATTENDING PHYSICIAN: Dr. Sarah Jenkins, MD, PhD. DIAGNOSIS: Malignant neoplasm of prostate (cT2b N0 M0), Gleason 7 (4+3). TREATMENT PLANNING PROCESS: The patient underwent CT simulation in the supine position with a customized immobilization device (Knee-Lok and foot support) and a comfortably full bladder. The CT dataset was imported into the Eclipse treatment planning system. CONTOURING: I personally reviewed and approved all target volumes and organs at risk (OARs). Gross Tumor Volume (GTV): Prostate gland. Clinical Target Volume (CTV): Prostate and proximal seminal vesicles. Planning Target Volume (PTV): CTV + 0.5 cm margin (0.3 cm posteriorly). OARs contoured: Bladder, rectum, penile bulb, and bilateral femoral heads. PLAN DESIGN & DOSIMETRY: A 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy (3D-CRT) plan was generated. Multiple coplanar 15 MV photon beams were arranged to optimize target coverage while minimizing dose to the adjacent critical structures. DOSE PRESCRIPTION: Total Dose: 79.2 Gy. Fractionation: 1.8 Gy per fraction x 44 fractions. PLAN EVALUATION: Dose-volume histograms (DVH) were generated and critically evaluated. PTV coverage: >95% of the PTV receives 100% of the prescription dose. Rectum: V70 < 20%, V50 < 50%. Bladder: V70 < 30%, V50 < 50%. Femoral heads: Max dose < 45 Gy. All normal tissue constraints have been met. The 3D treatment plan is approved for clinical use. The patient will proceed with QA and first treatment delivery. Electronically signed by: Sarah Jenkins, MD, PhD.
documents.Justification: The documentation supports the requested CPT code 77215 for radiotherapy treatment planning. The note details the importation of CT simulation data, physician contouring of the GTV, CTV, PTV, and organs at risk (bladder, rectum, femoral heads). It further describes the generation of a 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy plan, beam arrangement, and the physician's critical evaluation of the dose-volume histograms (DVH) to ensure target coverage and normal tissue constraints were met prior to approving the plan.
